question: What is the main purpose of pipelining in a CPU?
choices: To divide instruction processing into stages and overlap the stages of different instructions, increasing throughput
To always shorten the execution time (latency) of each instruction
To reduce the number of instructions and make programs smaller
explanation: Pipelining overlaps stages such as fetch, decode, execute and write-back like an assembly line, increasing the number of instructions completed per unit time (throughput). It does not shorten the processing time of each instruction itself, and the flow can be disrupted by branches and data dependencies (hazards).

question: What is the main purpose of cache memory?
choices: To retain data when the power is turned off
To keep frequently used data close to the CPU and bridge the speed gap with main memory
To correct errors in computation results
explanation: Accessing main memory (DRAM) is slow compared with the CPU's processing speed, so frequently used data and instructions are kept in fast caches (mainly SRAM) to reduce waiting time. Caches exploit the tendency of programs to reuse data from nearby times and addresses (locality).

question: Which is a characteristic of a von Neumann computer?
choices: Instructions and data are always kept in separate memories
Programs (instructions) and data are stored in the same main memory, and instructions are read and executed in order
explanation: In the von Neumann (stored-program) architecture, instructions and data are kept in the same main memory, and the CPU reads and executes instructions in sequence. An architecture with separate memories and paths for instructions and data is the Harvard architecture, used in microcontrollers and DSPs, and also in the cache organization inside CPUs.

question: What is the main purpose of putting multiple processor cores on one chip (multicore)?
choices: To increase performance per watt through parallel processing
To eliminate the need for an instruction set
To eliminate the need for main memory
explanation: Continuing to raise clock frequency made power consumption and heat too great, so the industry moved toward raising performance by sharing work across multiple cores. To get the benefit, however, software must also be able to split its work into parallel tasks.

question: Which is a characteristic of RISC (reduced instruction set computer)?
choices: It has many complex instructions of varying length
It limits instructions to a small number of simple ones, making pipelining easier
It has no instructions at all
explanation: RISC is a design philosophy that limits instructions to simple ones of uniform length so that each can execute in a short time. Because instruction processing times are uniform, it is well suited to pipelining. An architecture with complex, multifunction instructions is called CISC.

question: What is the period of a 1 GHz clock?
explanation: The period is the reciprocal of the frequency. 1 GHz = 10⁹ Hz, so the period is 1 / 10⁹ = 10⁻⁹ s = 1 ns. In that 1 ns, light travels only about 30 cm.

question: What is the purpose of branch prediction in a CPU?
choices: To predict the outcome of branch instructions and execute ahead, reducing pipeline stalls
To predict power consumption and control the power supply
explanation: In a pipeline, the next instruction to execute is not known until the branch outcome is determined, so processing stalls. Branch prediction predicts the branch target from past history and continues execution, redoing work only when the prediction is wrong. Prediction accuracy has a large effect on performance.

question: What is the main reason GPUs are well suited to matrix operations and AI training and inference?
choices: Their clock frequency is over 100 times that of CPUs
They have many simple arithmetic units and can process large amounts of data in parallel
explanation: GPUs were originally designed to process many image pixels at once, with thousands of simple arithmetic units arranged in parallel. For workloads that repeat the same calculation on large amounts of data, such as matrix operations, they deliver high performance by exploiting this parallelism.

question: If the cache access time is 10 ns, the main memory access time is 100 ns, and the cache hit rate is 90%, what is the average access time?
explanation: Average access time = hit rate × cache access time + (1 − hit rate) × main memory access time = 0.9 × 10 + 0.1 × 100 = 9 + 10 = 19 ns. A small drop in hit rate greatly lengthens the average access time, so cache design directly affects performance.

question: In a CMOS circuit, if only the supply voltage is halved with everything else unchanged, what happens to dynamic power consumption?
explanation: Dynamic power in CMOS circuits is P = α C V² f (α: activity factor, C: load capacitance, V: supply voltage, f: frequency), proportional to the square of the supply voltage. Halving the voltage reduces power to one quarter. Lowering voltage is therefore the most effective way to save power, but it reduces operating speed.

question: What do names like ARM, x86 and RISC-V mainly refer to?
explanation: These are names of instruction set architectures (ISAs), which define the contract between software and hardware, such as the types and formats of instructions a processor understands. With the same ISA, processors designed by different companies can run the same programs.

question: Which is a characteristic of RISC-V?
choices: It is a proprietary instruction set that only one company can use
It is an instruction set exclusively for GPUs
It is an instruction set architecture with an open specification that can be used without license fees
explanation: RISC-V is an open instruction set architecture whose development began at a university. Its specification is public and anyone can use it without license fees, so many companies and research institutions have adopted it, for everything from embedded microcontrollers to high-performance processors.

question: What is the processor design called that issues and executes multiple instructions simultaneously in one clock cycle?
explanation: A superscalar processor has multiple execution units and executes independent instructions simultaneously, increasing the number of instructions executed per clock. Combined with out-of-order execution and similar techniques, it is used in high-performance CPUs.

question: Which cache holds the results of translating virtual addresses into physical addresses to speed up address translation?
explanation: Virtual memory requires translating the virtual addresses used by programs into physical addresses in memory. The translation tables (page tables) are in memory, so looking them up every time would be slow; the TLB keeps recently used translations for fast translation.

question: Which dedicated circuit is built into smartphone SoCs and similar chips to perform AI inference quickly and with low power?
explanation: An NPU is a dedicated circuit for efficiently performing the multiply-accumulate operations that make up most of the computation in neural networks. It delivers higher performance per watt than a general-purpose CPU, allowing tasks such as image and speech recognition to be processed on the smartphone itself.

question: In a typical computer, which lists the memory hierarchy from fastest to slowest access?
choices: SSD → main memory → L2 cache → L1 cache → registers
Main memory → registers → SSD → L1 cache
Registers → L1 cache → L2 cache → main memory (DRAM) → SSD
explanation: Memory closer to the CPU is faster and smaller; memory farther away is slower, larger and cheaper. A hierarchy of registers, L1/L2/L3 caches (SRAM), main memory (DRAM) and storage (SSD, etc.) keeps frequently used data in the faster levels, achieving memory that is fast and large overall.

question: Approximately how many instructions per second can a processor with a 2 GHz clock and an average CPI (clocks per instruction) of 0.5 execute?
explanation: There are 2×10⁹ clocks per second, and each instruction takes 0.5 clocks on average, so the number of instructions is 2×10⁹ ÷ 0.5 = 4×10⁹, or 4 billion. A CPI below 1 means multiple instructions are executed per clock, for example by a superscalar design.

question: If 90% of a program can be parallelized, what is the theoretical maximum speedup when it runs on an unlimited number of processors?
explanation: According to Amdahl's law, the part that cannot be parallelized (10%) does not get shorter no matter how many processors are added, so the total execution time cannot fall below 10% of the original. The maximum speedup is therefore 1 ÷ 0.1 = 10 times. This shows the importance of reducing the non-parallelizable part.

question: Which scheme performs the same operation on multiple data items simultaneously with a single instruction?
explanation: SIMD (single instruction, multiple data) performs the same operation on multiple data items in parallel with one instruction. It is effective for image processing and matrix operations, and many CPUs provide SIMD instructions. GPUs also process large amounts of data in parallel using an approach similar to SIMD.

question: Which CPU configuration combines high-performance cores and power-efficient cores and uses them according to the workload?
choices: Heterogeneous configuration combining cores of different performance (such as big.LITTLE)
explanation: Heavy tasks run quickly on high-performance cores, while light and background tasks run on power-efficient cores, balancing performance and battery life. This approach spread in smartphone processors and has also been adopted in PC CPUs.

question: Which technique examines instruction dependencies and executes ready instructions in an order different from the program order to improve performance?
explanation: In out-of-order execution, instructions waiting for earlier results are postponed and later instructions that are ready run first. This makes better use of execution units and raises performance, but it requires mechanisms such as committing results in program order, making the circuitry more complex.

question: Which CPU mechanism temporarily suspends the current task to give priority to handling requests such as those from external devices?
explanation: When an event such as keyboard input, a timer or received data occurs, an interrupt makes the CPU suspend its current task, run the corresponding handler, and then return to the original task. The CPU no longer needs to keep checking the status of peripherals.

question: Which mechanism transfers data directly between peripherals and memory without going through the CPU?
explanation: With DMA, a dedicated controller transfers data between memory and peripherals, so the CPU can continue with other work during the transfer. It is used where large amounts of data are moved, such as storage and networking.

question: Which LSI integrates a CPU, memory and peripherals such as timers and ADCs on one chip and is used to control appliances and equipment?
explanation: A microcontroller integrates, besides the CPU, flash memory for programs, working RAM, timers, ADCs, communication interfaces and more on one chip. It is used to control all kinds of equipment, including appliances, cars and industrial machinery, and is shipped in very large quantities.

question: In a multicore CPU, which mechanism keeps data consistent when the caches of several cores hold data for the same address?
explanation: If one core updates data in its cache while old data remains in other cores' caches, those cores would use wrong values. Cache coherence control keeps data consistent across all cores, for example by notifying other cores of the update and invalidating their stale copies.

question: Which technique reduces CPU power consumption by dynamically changing operating frequency and supply voltage according to the load?
explanation: DVFS lowers frequency and supply voltage when the load is light and raises them when it is heavy. Dynamic power is proportional to the square of the voltage and to frequency, so lowering both together greatly reduces power. It is widely used in smartphones and laptops.

question: Which is an example of vulnerabilities revealing attacks that exploit traces of speculative execution left in the cache to infer data that should not be accessible?
explanation: Spectre and Meltdown, disclosed in 2018, exploit the fact that even when the results of speculatively executed work are discarded, traces remain in the cache state, allowing secret data to be inferred from differences in access time. They showed that mechanisms for improving performance can become security weaknesses.

question: Which metric indicates the amount of heat generated under a standard heavy load, used as a guide for CPU cooling design?
explanation: TDP (thermal design power) is the heat output used as a guide for designing CPU cooling, expressed in watts (W). Cooling systems are designed to remove TDP worth of heat. Some mechanisms allow running above TDP for short periods to boost performance.

question: Which metric indicates the number of instructions executed per clock?
explanation: IPC (instructions per clock) is the average number of instructions executed per clock and is the reciprocal of CPI (clocks per instruction). At the same clock frequency, higher IPC means higher performance. Superscalar and out-of-order execution are techniques for raising IPC.

question: What is the problem called in which power and heat constraints prevent all circuits on a chip from running at full performance at the same time?
explanation: With the end of Dennard scaling, power per transistor no longer drops enough even as transistor counts increase. Running all circuits on a chip at once would exceed the allowable heat, so some must be idled. This is called dark silicon, and it is part of the background for designs that use specialized circuits for different tasks.
